Subject: Optimizer Toolkit — pricing, batch/cache & quantization asks

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for last week's demo — Zipline's infra and product team liked the performance profiles. Before we move to an internal exec review, procurement and engineering need a compact picture of the commercial and technical tradeoffs so we can compare options. Specifically: 

1) Pricing: can you confirm a succinct pricing ladder for the Optimize Toolkit add-on (credits vs committed) and a sample quote for a 6-month pilot with 500M tokens/month?

2) Batching & cache guidance: engineering asked how Redwood recommends configuring batching and KV/prefix caching for a chat-heavy workload (avg seq length 150, 95th 450). Any guardrails or expected latency impact?

3) Quantization: what quantization profiles do you recommend for the pilot to balance cost and occasional quality-sensitive responses? Any estimated unit-cost reduction by profile?

If helpful, I attached our draft Mutual Action Plan (zipline_mop_draft.docx) to show timelines. We need answers in time for our vendor short-list by EOD Thursday.

—Jonah
Procurement, Zipline AI

Jonah — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary here and we'll follow with a short technical note from Rishi. I attached a one-page quote and a short quantization primer (redwood_quant_recs.pdf).

Pricing (high level)
- Pilot credits (6 months, 500M tokens/month): we can offer an evaluation bundle of 2.75B tokens as committed credits with a 30% pilot discount on Optimize Toolkit fees.
- Post-pilot options: pay-as-you-go (credits) or a committed band with stepped discounts at 12/24/36 month tenure.
- Example: for the pilot above, list economics are in the attached one-pager; net after the pilot discount, the per-token optimized cost is ~0.65x baseline (depends on config).

Batching & caching guidance (ops-safe defaults)
- Start with conservative batching: target 40–60ms added queue time to keep p95 latency SLAs intact. For chat workloads, use max_batch_size tuned to percentile of concurrent active requests (we can run a traffic-simulation quickly).
- KV/prefix caching: enable prefix caching for the 70% of requests that are short-turn single-prompt calls. For longer interactions (avg seq 150 / 95th 450), configure a dynamic eviction window (TTL per conversation of ~20–30s) to avoid unnecessary memory pressure.
- Guardrails: set a fallback on batch timeout (e.g., 80ms) to ensure interactive flows don't spike. We'll include preset profiles in the pilot for you to A/B.

Next steps: Rishi will add recommended quant profiles and expected % savings per profile. If that looks good, we can lock the pilot quote and ship an ops-runbook for Day 0. I can also jump on a 30-min call Wednesday to finalize the MOP.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Optimizer Toolkit — pricing, batch/cache & quantization asks

Jonah/Asha — quick technical addendum with recommended quant/batching/caching settings you can try in the pilot. High level conclusions up front: int8 (GPT-style symmetric) + prefix KV cache yields the best cost/quality balance for your workload; int4 is viable for non-critical paths and can push marginal token cost down further but increases hallucination risk on rare long-form answers.

Quantization recommendations
- Default: int8 dynamic range for decoder layers (recommended for the pilot). Expected unit-cost reduction: ~25–30% vs FP16 inference on the same hardware when paired with our optimized kernels.
- Aggressive saving: int4 (4-bit) mixed-mode for embeddings and early layers with selective FP16 for last 2 layers — yields additional ~10–15% on top of int8 in synthetic benchmarks, but quality degradation observed on ~1–3% of samples in our eval set (long-context retrieval + citation cases).
- Safety: enable per-request "high-fidelity" flag for the small subset of calls (e.g., payment confirmation, legal copy) so they run on FP16 or int8-high-precision paths.

Batching & KV/prefix caching specifics
- Batching: use a latency-aware scheduler with a target micro-batch latency of 30–50ms for p50 and a hard cap at 120ms. This matches your seq distribution and keeps end-user latency acceptable.
- KV cache policy: enable streaming KV reuse across the session and a prefix cache keyed on user prompt canonicalization. For your average seq = 150 we saw 18–24% token compute reduction; for bursts with repeated prompts reuse can hit 35–40%.
- Eviction/consistency: for multi-region failover, prefer time-based TTL over LRU to avoid cross-replica thrash. Configure a warmup grace period after cold-starts to reduce early tail latency.

Operational notes
- We'll provide a pilot config bundle (three presets: conservatively optimized, balanced, and aggressive-savings) so your SRE can toggle settings without redeploying.
- Instrumentation: enable token-level cost breakdown and per-route quality flags so we can quantify regressions during the pilot and roll back aggressive quant profiles automatically.

I'll attach a short lab report with benchmarks if you want more numbers; happy to run with a trimmed subset of your prompts to give Zipline-specific estimates.

—Rishi
Staff Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
